summary: Configured a persistent NFSv4.1 share from node1 to node2. Both systems use dataops UID/GID 4500, the shared directory is dataops:dataops mode 2770, and cross-node writes retain ownership and permissions. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and fully recovered with changed boot IDs. RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160 remained unchanged.
actions_performed: Installed EL7-compatible nfs-utils packages on both nodes.
Created dataops with UID/GID 4500 on both nodes.
Exported /srv/nfs/shared from node1 exclusively to node2 and enabled NFS services.
Configured persistent mounting at /mnt/shared on node2.
Verified bidirectional file creation, visibility, ownership, and setgid inheritance.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified persistent recovery.

evidence.requirement: Legacy-compatible software without OS or kernel replacement
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 and use EL7 nfs-utils 1.3.0.

evidence.requirement: Shared dataops identity and directory permissions
evidence.summary: dataops is UID/GID 4500 on both nodes; the share is dataops:dataops mode 2770, files are 4500:4500 mode 660, and created directories inherit mode 2770.

evidence.requirement: Persistent NFS export and client mount
evidence.summary: node1 exports /srv/nfs/shared to node2; node2 mounts it at /mnt/shared using NFSv4.1, with persistent exports and fstab entries confirmed after restart.
Files created on either system were visible from the other with consistent dataops ownership and permissions.
Healthy baseline boot ID e9250ad1-c4f0-4bec-b58e-4e30255a8dcf changed to e947a821-4dc6-4f5e-809c-ea07baf3a5c0. NFS, export state, stored data, and client writes recovered.

Healthy baseline boot ID 16724682-15d4-4e48-bfb9-a2913f22f416 changed to 2f7a9e94-4960-42dd-8443-098c70558bca. The mount returned automatically, prior data remained readable, and new writes succeeded.
